625-bae-system.name: BEL-SYNC (BAE hub — Syncbox/SCU3 sync & disconnect logic)
625-bae-system.why: Resolved mapping: BEL-SYNC -> 625-bae-system. The Syncbox terminal strip, its 'BEL-SYNC CBx.11 5A' fuse tap toward LVPDU, and the sync/return conductors to BEL1-P/BEL2-P/BEL1-S/BEL2-S I/O blocks are the hub-level logic tying all four BEL converters together for synchronised paralleling.

fns.label: BEL synchronisation and disconnect control logic
fns.what: Provides the common sync/disconnect signalling backbone (Syncbox) that lets the four BEL converters (PORT BEL-1/2, STBD BEL-1/2) be paralleled and monitored together as one AC bus, with trip inputs back from each BEL and a 24V sync feed/return pair routed toward the LVPDU.
fns.dry: Fused terminal rating 5A on the 24V sync feed to LVPDU; module identity Syncbox/SCU3 P51 per sheet labels.
kc: Syncbox terminal strip (GR and BLK groups)
SCU3 terminal strip (P51) cross-wired to Syncbox
BEL1-P, BEL2-P, BEL1-S, BEL2-S I/O terminal blocks (pins 3, 7)
fused terminal 'BEL-SYNC CBx.11 5A' feeding onward to LVPDU
sc: default/sync

Syncbox GR pins 1-4 (G3-21xx BEL1-4 Disconnect) and pins 12/11/10/9 (BEL1-P/2-P/3-S/4-S TRIP) cross-wire to SCU3 P51 pins 9/11/12/6/24; Syncbox BLK pins 1-4 (G3-S1S2..S4S2 SYNC) and 12/11/10/9 (SYNC RTN) route to each BEL's I/O pins 3/7, closing the loop that lets SCU3 command disconnect/trip and read sync status per BEL converter
24V sync supply onward
Syncbox +6/-7 (24V-SYNC P/R) -> fused terminal 'BEL-SYNC CBx.11 5A' -> onward to LVPDU (cross-reference, not detailed on this sheet)

fns.label: HVIL (High Voltage Interlock Loop) safety chain
fns.what: A series safety interlock loop threaded through every HV device connector (BEL1, BEL2, EDN, MAPS, MPCS, and the port/stbd bus isolator) — each HVIL contact is normally-open and must be made (device connector correctly seated/interlocked) for the loop to complete; the loop is used to disable the HV bus if any connector or panel is opened. G3-K320/K321 (port) and G3-K420/K421 (stbd) are the MPCS HVIL IN/OUT taps that close this loop through the MPCS LV2 connector.
fns.dry: HVIL loop, NO contacts throughout, confirmed by wiring measurement on this sheet
kc: HVIL switch contacts (NO) at BEL1, BEL2, EDN, MAPS, isolator, MPCS connectors (both sides)
sc: interlock made (normal, HV enabled)

Port bus HVIL feed -> series NO contacts at BEL1-P, BEL2-P, EDN, MAPS-P, isolator, and MPCS-P (G3-K320 IN / G3-K321 OUT) -> loop continuity confirmed -> HV bus permitted energised; mirrored on STBD via G3-K420/K421
interlock broken
Any HVIL contact opens (connector disconnected/panel open) -> loop path breaks -> HV bus disabled/tripped (per BAE system design; exact trip logic off-sheet)

fns.label: [infrastructure] MPCS-P / MPCS-S LV2 terminal strips and MOTOR sensor wiring (shared BAE monitoring backbone)
sc: MPCS-P LV2 and MPCS-S LV2 terminal strips wire HVIL, position sensor A/B, position excitation, and stator temperature signals to their respective SWITCH PORT / SWITCH STBD terminal strips, which connect onward to the shared MOTOR M1.
Both port and stbd terminal strips are mirror layouts (pins 1-13, 23, 30-31) with identical signal roles, differing only in G3-K3xx (port) vs G3-K4xx (stbd) tag numbering.

fns.label: [infrastructure] Battery Fuse and Isolator Panel (24V start batteries)
sc: Houses four 24V/200Ah battery banks (GMDSS, Emergency, Gen Start, Aux Service) each with its own shunt for current monitoring and paired fuses for charger/inverter/start feeds.
Negative bus rail runs across the panel returning all four battery negatives.
This panel and the adjacent Battery Isolator Panel (dashed box, SW11-SW16) are shared BAE-system LV start infrastructure — not a distinct equipment node.

fns.label: [infrastructure] Battery Isolator Panel (generator start selection)
sc: Dashed-boundary box containing selector switches SW11-SW16 that route the Gen Start battery (via SO9 relay contact) to either PORT or STBD generator B+ start circuit through CB1/CB2 50A breakers and fuse '70' each side.
Outputs also continue 'to CBI Control' off to another part of the sheet/drawing.

fns.label: [infrastructure] LVPDU (Low Voltage Power Distribution Unit) main bus/rack
sc: 24V/110A AC-DC converter (230VAC in) feeds F18 125A fuse -> CT5 -> SW5 isolator, continuing off-sheet per 'see DWG 110a'.
SHUNT #1 (500A/50mV) -> F9 125A -> SW10 also continues off-sheet 'see DWG 110a'.
CT6/SHUNT#5 feed ammeter (A) and voltmeter (V) instrumentation and report current/voltage to ONYX monitoring.
PORT and STBD breaker columns (CB1-CB23, CBx1-CBx20) hang off this LVPDU bus via F2A fuse, distributing 24V to all the named BAE-system loads listed in equipment_groups.

Established note block: LVPDU=Low Voltage Power Distribution; ISG=Integrated Starter/Generator System; SCU=System Control Unit; MPCS=Modular Propulsion Control System; ESS=Energy Storage System; EDN=Shore Charger 400V 3Ph/600V DC; MAPS=Modular Auxiliary Power System 600V DC/24V DC; HMI=Screen; ACTM=Propulsion Motor; EMRAX=Hydraulic Pump Motor.

620-hvpdu.name: PORT/STBD HVPDU (600V DC bus, isolation and paralleling)
620-hvpdu.why: Sheet title 'SWS 600V HIGH VOLTAGE HVPDU' and the PORT/STBD 600V DC BUS boxes with breakers Q1-Q4, fuses F1-F12, and the center ISOLATOR are the core subject of this drawing; established fact confirms the 600V DC bus bars ARE the HVPDU.

fns.label: [infrastructure] PORT/STBD HVPDU (600V DC bus, isolation and paralleling)
sc: PORT HVPDU and STBD HVPDU each present a 600V DC bus (+/-) with Q1 32A and Q2 32A breakers feeding BEL-1 and BEL-2 respectively, plus F1 500A / F2 500A fuses on the incoming bus per the established HVPDU identity fact.
The 230V AC outputs of all four BELs pass through isolators S1-S4 (25A each) and relay contacts K1-K4/Re1-Re4 to build the common 230V AC BUS (L1/N) shown at top-right.

Relay bank Re aux1-4 and contactors K1-K4 sequence/interlock the isolators building the 230V AC bus; per measured netlist all are NO contacts (load off until coil energised), consistent with a start/paralleling-permissive scheme.

A current transformer (CT) is in series on the 230V AC bus feed near L2, with an onward reference 'see DWG 102' and 'see DWG 113' for continuation of that AC line and a T/S A terminal group (BAE/AUX/+EM taps).

fns.label: Port/Stbd 600V DC bus distribution with breaker/fuse protected outfeeds
fns.what: Distributes 600V DC from the port and stbd HV DC buses to each downstream load (BEL1, BEL2, EDN, MAPS, ESS #1/2/3, MPCS, and the propulsion MOTOR windings) via dedicated breakers (Q1-Q4, 32A each) and fuses (F3-F12, 200-400A) per feed; a center ISOLATOR (F1/F2 500A fused) ties port and stbd buses together for fault isolation between the two DC systems.
fns.dry: 600V DC bus, port + stbd; Q1-Q4 32A breakers; F1/F2 500A isolator fuses; F3/F4 200A; F5/F6 400A; F7/F8 400A; F9-F12 200A; conductor 2x2/0 typical outfeed, 4/0 motor conductors
sc: normal
PORT 600V DC BUS (NEG/POS) -> Q1-Q4 32A breakers -> BEL1-P/BEL2-P/EDN-P/MAPS-P feeds; and -> F3-F6 200-400A fuses -> ESS#1/MPCS/M1P motor windings (4/0 conductors) -> MOTOR M1

fns.what: A center 'MPCS A/C SELECTION' switch block selects which MPCS (port or stbd) drives the shared MOTOR M1 windings (M1-A/M1-B/M1-C), per established identity fact that S2 selects which MPCS drives the ACTM.

fns.label: [infrastructure] 600V DC Bus Bars (Port + Stbd) and Isolator
sc: Per established identity fact: the 600V DC bus bars ARE the HVPDU's high-voltage buses; never model as separate 'backbone' system.
Center ISOLATOR ties port and stbd 600V DC buses via F1/F2 500A fuses, allowing fault isolation between sides.
Bus breakers Q1-Q4 (32A) feed BEL1/BEL2/EDN/MAPS per side; F3-F12 fuses (200-400A) feed ESS/MPCS/motor per side.

fns.label: [infrastructure] HVPDU (Port + Stbd) — 600V DC bus, breakers, fusing
sc: PORT HVPDU and STBD HVPDU each carry a 600V DC BUS with four breakers Q1-Q4 (32A each) feeding the respective MAPS-1/2 converters.
Each HVPDU side also has a 500A fuse pair (F1/F2 500A) protecting the 600V bus, per CTB legend QI-POWER-485-300-LV modules (CTB1-CTB7, CTB7 tied to EMERGENCY BAT.).
600V DC buses are isolated port/stbd (per established HVPDU identity fact); this sheet shows the 24V DC service-supply side downstream of the MAPS converters.

641-vessel-control-panel.name: Main GM Control Panel indicator supply (PC CARD #2 / QE7 emergency feed)

fns.label: [infrastructure] Main GM Control Panel indicator supply (PC CARD #2 / QE7 emergency feed)
sc: PC CARD #2 (labelled 'on main panel') carries a bank of indicator lamps (BAE/AUX/NEG/+EM legends) with GM logic module tying terminal groups 1-10 on each side.

The PC CARD #2 / GM indicator block's supply passes through terminal strip T/S E way 8/8a, through breaker QE7 6A (AUX 1), then onward 'to +24V EMERGENCY POWER' — consistent with the established fact that QE7 powers the main GM panel indicators.
T/S A and T/S B terminal strips (BAE/AUX/+EM legends, positions 5-9 and 1-4) carry these same tags onward with cross-references 'see DWG 113' for continuation.

fns.label: [infrastructure] AC DB PANEL bus/breaker structure and metering (230V AC BUS)
sc: 230V AC BUS with L1/N feeds nine group breakers #1-#9, each 63A except #7 which is also 63A (AFT OUTLETS), each with an inline current transformer CT1-CT9 for metering.
Group breaker assignments as printed: #1 SERVICES, #2 SERVICES, #3 AIR-CON, #4 ENTERTAINMENT, #5 CHARGERS, #6 BAE COOLING, #7 AFT OUTLETS, #8 GALLEY 1, #9 GALLEY 2.
#5 CHARGERS, #6 BAE COOLING, #8 GALLEY 1, #9 GALLEY 2 feed onward via multi-core cable to further panels — these branches are cross-references, not detailed on this sheet.
100A AUX POWER SUPPLY breaker feeds an outgoing feeder off-sheet (separate from the #1-#9 group breakers).

Earth Leakage breakers 1-13 sit downstream of the group breakers, each protecting a sub-bank of Q-numbered branch breakers (e.g. EARTH LEAKAGE 4 feeds Q1-Q4 and also Q7-Q13 area; EARTH LEAKAGE 5/6/7 feed START BAT./EMERGENCY BAT./GMDSS BAT. chargers; EARTH LEAKAGE 8-12 feed PORT/STBD/CPP seawater cooling and CPP oil/oil-boost circuits — those loads are cross-references to their own equipment, see below).

13 CTA tags (CTA1-CTA13) are all logged simply as 'QI-POWER-485' — a monitoring bus tag repeated identically for every CT, appears to be a monitoring/telemetry protocol reference rather than distinct data, kept as infrastructure note.
A 205kW inverter (24VDC in / 230VAC out, per DWG 110c cross-reference) supplies a downstream branch feeding Q34-Q38 loads (ESS ventilation, WiFi, Starlink, spares) via its own EARTH LEAKAGE 13 (10A).

fns.label: [infrastructure] Main Panel Terminal/Plug Distribution (T/S E, T/S F, T/S C, PLUG A/B/C, PC CARD)
sc: T/S E and T/S F terminal strips interconnect via multi-core cables MU5-12 and MU4-12 (12 wires each), consistent with the established wiring_note fact.
PLUG A, PLUG B, PLUG C are the panel's main connector groups routing to PC CARD (dotted-line box) which hosts diode arrays driving the indicator lamp bank.
Terminal 12/69 and terminal 119/120 are marked 'not used' — spares, not in use (consistent with established fact).
AUX PLUG ON PC BOARD is cross-referenced to 'see DWG 114' for its continuation.
XA41 and XA61 terminal taps are STATUS OUT taps (no coil on their nets per measured netlist) feeding the Onyx/monitoring system, not control commands into this panel.
PC CARD diode array acts as a common isolation/OR-ing network feeding the indicator lamp bank from multiple fused terminal sources.

fns.label: [infrastructure] DC Main Panel & FWD DC Panel distribution (bilge/fire pump breaker feeds)
sc: DC MAIN PANEL: F3 60A/SW8 feeds Main Bilge Pump SO6 loop; F4 100A/SW9 feeds Main Fire Pump SO7 loop.
FWD DC PANEL (see DWG 120): Q2 10A feeds Aux Mast Bilge Pump Re2 loop; Q3 10A feeds Aux Engine Room Bilge Pump Re3 loop.
T/S S terminal strip banks (1-3, 13-15, 16-19) and T/S F terminal strip (11-16) are local terminal distribution for these loops, physically on/near the DC Main Panel and FWD DC Panel.
F5 100A fuse feeds +24V SERVICE SUPPLY bus that in turn supplies T/S B and onward to T/S E/C terminal strips.

T/S B, T/S E (terminal 8, fed from EMERGENCY BAT +24V), and T/S C (terminals 1-6 wired to PORT/STBD XA41 and XA61 taps) form a terminal-strip chain routing +24V service and emergency battery supply plus ONYX XA-tap signals toward the MAIN PANEL PC CARD alarm module.
MU4-12 multi-core cable runs vertically through the sheet carrying the T/S B/C/E/F terminal signals between panel sections.

fns.label: [infrastructure] DC Main Panel — terminal strips, relays and SR2 module (infrastructure)
sc: Terminal strip T/S B (terminals 31-39) is fed from breaker Q16 (FUEL/VENTILATION, 10A); terminal 37 tied to SCREEN (shield ground).

fns.label: [infrastructure] Main Panel PC Card — Bilge/Fire alarm annunciator
sc: MAIN PANEL PC CARD block (dotted box) receives inputs from T/S C terminals 1-6 (PORT XA41-04, STBD XA41-02, XA41-06, XA61-30, XA61-28, XA61-26) via a diode bank/diode bridge array, driving five indicator lamps labelled LAZARETTE BILGE, AFT BILGE, ENGINE ROOM BILGE, FWD BILGE, SAIL LOCKER — this is a bilge-level alarm annunciator, not part of any single pump's own loop.
The card also drives an ALARM MOD (horn/speaker) with MUTE (S15) and TEST (S14) pushbuttons.
T/S C terminals 19/20 feed RUN IND. lamps for MAST BILGE and AUX ENGINE pump run-status (see aux-bilge-run-indicators function above) into this same card.

XA41 and XA61 taps on this sheet are measured as STATUS (no coil on their nets) per the tag-direction analysis — i.e., these are status-out reports into the Onyx/monitoring card, not commands driving relays on this sheet.

sc: Fieldbus coupler X0 = WAGO 750-362, with X1 filter module 750-626 immediately after it.

Positions 05-06 = analog input modules WAGO 750-455 (AI1, AI2); position 07 = analog input WAGO 750-457 (AI3).
Position 08 = DO1, module WAGO 750-1504 (a distinct DO type from the 750-508 group used elsewhere on the rack).
X2 = POWER SUPPLY module 750-602, feeding the following DO group: positions 09-13 (DO2-DO6), all WAGO 750-508.
X3 = POWER SUPPLY module 750-602, feeding positions 14-18 (DO7-DO11), all WAGO 750-508.
X4 = POWER SUPPLY module 750-602, feeding positions 19-23 (DO12-DO16), all WAGO 750-508.
X5 = BUS EXTENSION END MODULE 750-627, closing the first physical rack row.
X6 = BUS EXTENSION COUPLER MODULE 750-628, opening a second physical rack row (extension across the bus).

Second row: positions 24-28 (DO17-DO21), all WAGO 750-508, no dedicated power supply shown before them on this row (fed via X6 bus extension coupling back to upstream power, or via X7 further down the row).
X7 = POWER SUPPLY module 750-602, feeding positions 29-32 (DO22-DO25, WAGO 750-508) and position 33 (AO1, WAGO 750-559) — consistent with the engineer red-pen fact already on this node.
X8 = END MODULE 750-600, terminating the second row.

CPU/coupler module shows dip-switch address bank (1-8, ON/1, '0:WBM / 255:DHCP' addressing modes), dual Ethernet ports (LINK/ACT indicators x2), MS/NS/I2O status LEDs, and 24V/0V power input terminals with +/- and fuse pairs (F1/F2) at coupler and at each power-supply module (X2-X4, X7).

Each DO module (750-508 type) is a 2-channel output module with A1/A2 coil-style terminal pairs per channel and an 'M' (common) reference terminal per module pair — consistent with the WAGO commons convention (M = per-module common/reference).
The rack is split across two physical DIN rows joined by the X5/X6 bus-extension pair, per the drawing's own bus-extension end/coupler module labels.

This is the INDEX/GA page for the MAST rack per the engineer red-pen note: individual module detail (channel-to-function mapping, e.g. DO2/DO3/DO4 = POS.09/10/11 per the vessel documentation excerpt referencing Main Cunningham/other sailing functions) is shown on subsequent detail pages (sheet 17 of 25 references POS.09-11 as DO-02/DO-03/DO-04), not on this index sheet.

520-bilge-system.name: Bilge & Fire System (system card)
520-bilge-system.why: The four operating modes and the overall bilge/fire main lines (main bilge line teal, fire line red, aux purple, emergency orange/green) describe the SYSTEM's lineups, not a single pump's, so they attach to the system card per the class rule.

fns.label: Normal operation: Main Bilge // Main Fire
fns.what: In normal running, the Main Bilge Pump clears whichever sump has water (only the NC valve for that sump area is opened) and discharges overboard via the anti-siphon manifold; independently the Electric Fire Pump (with Diesel Fire Pump as an alternative prime mover on the same suction) draws seawater via strainer and feeds the fire line in the port sheer to hydrants/hoses and the tender-garage sprinkler.
kc: motor-actuated NC bilge valves (5, one per sump area)
sc: normal bilge duty

selected sump (Lazarette/Midship/ER/Mast Area/Sail Locker) -> its NC motor-actuated valve (opened only for that sump) -> main bilge line -> Main Bilge Pump suction -> Main Bilge Pump discharge -> seawater strainer 005-03 -> anti-siphon manifold (breather to STBD E-R vent box) -> bilge overboard; all other sump valves remain NC/closed
normal fire duty
seawater pickup -> seawater strainer -> Electric Fire Pump (or Diesel Fire Pump alternative) -> fire line in port sheer (fwd + aft runs) -> fire hydrants / fire hoses / tender garage sprinkler head

fns.label: Auxiliary bilge operation — overboard (where regulations allow)
fns.what: The two auxiliary bilge pumps (E-R and Mast area) can independently pump their local sump overboard through an oily bilge filter, bypassing the main bilge pump, when permitted by regulation.
sc: aux overboard

Engine Room Sump or Mast Area Sump -> respective aux bilge pump suction -> pump discharge -> oily bilge filter -> flex suction hose connection -> FWD deck locker drain (min 800mm above DWL) -> overboard

fns.label: Auxiliary bilge operation — to portable storage containers
fns.what: Alternative discharge lineup for the same two aux bilge pumps, routing oily bilge water to portable oil storage tanks instead of overboard, via Gardena-type hose connections.
sc: aux to storage

Engine Room Sump or Mast Area Sump -> respective aux bilge pump -> oily bilge filter -> valved branch (item 021 Gardena connector) -> portable oil storage tank; FWD deck locker drain (below DWL) shown for reference only, not the active path

fns.label: Emergency operation — fire backup
fns.what: When the electric fire pump is not operational, the Diesel Fire Pump takes over fire-main duty alone, primed from the fresh-water supply.
kc: priming line from fresh water supply
sc: emergency fire (electric fire pump OUT)

seawater pickup -> seawater strainer -> Diesel Fire Pump (primed via priming line from fresh water supply, ref dwg 108-01-510-001) -> fire line in port sheer (both fore and aft sections) -> fire hydrants / hoses / tender garage sprinklers

fns.label: Emergency operation — bilge backup
fns.what: When the Main Bilge Pump is not operational, bilge duty is covered either by the Diesel Fire Pump (driven via the priming line, acting as bilge backup) or by the STBD Genset's raw water pump drawing from the sea chest, discharging via the exhaust water separator.
sc: emergency bilge (Main Bilge Pump OUT) — diesel fire pump as backup
selected sump (any of five, only its NC valve opened) -> main bilge line -> Diesel Fire Pump (via priming line) -> anti-siphon manifold (breather to STBD E-R vent box) -> bilge overboard
emergency bilge (Main Bilge Pump OUT) — genset raw water pump as backup
sea chest supply (ref dwg 108-01-515-003) -> STBD Genset raw water pump suction -> STBD Genset raw water pump discharge -> overboard via exhaust water separator (ref dwg 108-01-515-001)

520-diesel-fire-pump.name: Diesel Fire Pump
520-diesel-fire-pump.why: BOM item 002, Yanmar-engined Australian Pump unit, drawn as ICE-driven pump with manual pull-start, serving both fire and emergency bilge-backup duty per operating modes 1/3/4.

fns.label: Diesel fire/bilge-backup pump role-in-flow
fns.what: Manually (pull-start) driven diesel pump used both for normal fire-line duty (alongside the electric fire pump) and as the emergency backup for fire-main pressurisation or for bilge suction when the main bilge pump is out.
fns.dry: Flow rate 715 l/min (42.9 m3/h), 3.6 kW, max head 37m per Pump Data table.
kc: Diesel Fire Pump (BOM 002, Yanmar L48 diesel, Australian Pump RSEBUV/L48 NF 2")
sc: fire duty
seawater pickup -> strainer 005-01 -> Diesel Fire Pump suction -> discharge -> aft fire hydrant / fire line
emergency fire backup (electric fire pump out)
seawater pickup -> strainer -> Diesel Fire Pump (primed via priming line from fresh water supply, ref dwg 108-01-510-001) -> fire line in port sheer -> hydrants/hoses
emergency bilge backup (main bilge pump out)
main bilge line (from open sump valve) -> Diesel Fire Pump (via priming line) -> anti-siphon manifold -> bilge overboard
